mechanism_narrative: MET (RTK) and IL6ST/gp130 (cytokine receptor) are co-expressed in aged MuSC and myofibers. The rigid_helix_20 linker (~30 Å) forces close proximity between MET's kinase domain (residues 1078-1345) and IL6ST's intracellular domain (lacking intrinsic kinase). Under forced proximity, MET's kinase transphosphorylates IL6ST's membrane-proximal tyrosines, creating docking sites for STAT3 (canonical gp130 signal) and SHC1/GRB2/GAB1/PIK3R1 (MET's canonical RAS-PI3K adaptors). PLCG1/2 are sterically excluded because the rigid short helix prevents the large PLCG SH2-phospholipase module from bridging the MET-IL6ST geometry. FRS2/3 and IRS1/2 are excluded because IL6ST lacks the juxtamembrane TKB motif required for their docking. The biased output is MAPK+PI3K+STAT3 activation without PLCγ/Ca²⁺ signaling, producing a transcriptional program that upregulates muscle structural genes (ACTA2, MYL9, MYH11) and downregulates aged IEGs (EGR1, FOS, JUN) and sarcomeric stress markers (TTN, NEB, MYH9).
